Inputs: card #29410 (body, the claim comment 6579488343, the os-dev report 6580325941), PR #29436 (body, file list, net diff against main at the head), the check-runs on the head. Card eval premise re-read at origin/main a644163669: `REFUSED_PATH_FAMILIES` still refuses the bare collection there and `security-findings.md` section 3 still says the relay has no draft-create op; the premise holds and this diff changes both.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set, one new op: `advisory_create` in `OPS` — required `summary`, `description`, `packages`; optional `severity`, `cwe_ids`; `alone: true`; `permission: 'repository-advisories'`. RIGHT: shaped like `advisory_report`, and every other key (`vulnerabilities`, `vulnerable_version_range`, `patched_versions`, `ecosystem`, `cvss_vector_string`, `cve_id`, `start_private_fork`, `state`, `ghsa_id`, `credits`, `body`, `collaborators`) is refused by name in validate.mjs — the card's "no state other than draft, published unreachable, no credits, CVE request or private fork" is enforced at the validator, not asserted.
- Accept-set, one new field: `packages` in `FIELDS` — `list`, `quiet`, max 10, itemMax 214, `NPM_PACKAGE_SHAPE`. RIGHT: a quiet list is described by type and size on refusal (`describeQuietly`), never echoed; the shape refuses spaces, uppercase, a version or range after the name, a path, a URL and a bare scope (pinned); each name becomes exactly one `vulnerabilities` entry `{ package: { ecosystem: 'npm', name } }` and nothing else (pinned in validate.mjs and in the executor's exact-body case).
- Public surface, one new POST path: `REFUSED_PATH_FAMILIES`' advisory family goes from `(?!\/(?:GHSA…|reports)$)` to `(?!\/(?:GHSA…|reports)$|$)`, opening the bare collection `/repos/{o}/{r}/security-advisories` alone. RIGHT: a trailing slash, `?state=draft`, `?per_page=100`, `/x`, `x`, the CVE and fork tails stay refused (pinned); `ADVISORY_CREATE_PATH_SHAPE` is anchored `^/repos/[^/]+/[^/]+/security-advisories$`; and the whole-table pin now lists the four and only four security-advisories requests any row makes — the collection is reached by `advisory_create`'s POST and by no GET (the list is the same path under GET; no row spells that verb). The target repo is held to `TARGET_REPO_SHAPE`, so the path carries nothing of the payload.
- Grant: no change to `PERMISSIONS`, `STROKE_SCOPED_PERMISSIONS` or the mint step. RIGHT: `tokenPermissionsOf` reads the row's `permission`, so the new row mints `repository-advisories: write` for its stroke alone through the existing `permission_repository_advisories` output (pinned for all four rows, EMPTY for every other op); the workflow on origin/main reads that output and has ONE mint step, no un-narrowed fallback.
- Landing: `advisoryCreateReadBack` — 2xx with a shaped `ghsa_id` AND `state === 'draft'` lands; 2xx without id is UNCONFIRMED (never re-sent); 2xx in another state FAILED naming id and state in their shapes alone. RIGHT, and stricter than the report row (which accepts any state), which is what "published unreachable" needs on the create path.
- Executor routing: `adv || req.advisoryReport || req.advisoryCreate` sends the row to `confirmAdvisory`, so `resultOf` (which reads the answer's body) never sees a draft's answer; the row text is `advisoryCreateLandedText` (id, state, next stroke). RIGHT.
- Seat side: `ADVISORY_ANNOTATED_OPS` gains `advisory_create`, so the executor emits one `::notice` naming action, op and id, and the seat reads it back through the same parser and hands it on as `advisories` (`--json`). `CONTENT_CREATING_OPS` is derived from the table (`PROSE_KEYS` includes `summary`), so the draft is paced as content-creating under rule ⑤ without a listing. RIGHT; the dispatch.mjs edit is necessary, see ③.
- Rules: `security-findings.md` section 3 prefers `advisory_create` then `advisory_collaborators_add`, keeps `advisory_report`, records the per-account daily cap on new private reports, keeps "⛔ 席位永不以自身账号私报或写公告" and "发布归维护者", and sends a double refusal to the session hand-off with "⛔ 不换账号重发" (the rule-level spelling of `ADVISORY_ACCESS_REMEDY`); section 4 follows. `rest-channel.md` now points at `security-findings.md` instead of restating ("他处只指向本文" honoured). RIGHT as a rules change; one wording finding in ④.

### ② Semver level

- `skip-changeset` label, no changeset file. RIGHT: the six files are `.claude/**` and `scripts/pm/**`; nothing under `packages/` moves and no published package changes. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, both line-initial in the PR body; no changeset body to mirror them. RIGHT: no authorable key, value, meaning or default changes; the new field is a relay payload key, not metadata protocol.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation, `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` outside the claim's file surface: ANSWERED, necessary — `ADVISORY_ANNOTATED_OPS` is the only path by which a landed draft's id reaches the seat (the executor's `annotationFor` and the seat's `runAnnotationsFor` both read that list), and without it the seat could not run the follow-up `advisory_collaborators_add` the card's scope item 2 relies on. The seat battery pins the new entry (12 → 14 cases).
- Dev deviation, `rest-channel.md` advisory line loses its ✓: ANSWERED — the line now names an op no seat has called; the seat's live run (card Acceptance) restores it. No tree change needed.
- Dev deviation, `.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml` mint comment still says "THREE consumers": ANSWERED as a comment drift with a Tier H carrier; listed as should-fix in ④ with its carrier. The mint step itself needs no change (the validator's output drives it).
- Dev deviation, PR template headings folded into the os-dev section order: no contract effect.
- `open_questions: []`; `security_findings: none`; `out_of_scope_findings` names the workflow comment only. Nothing to escalate.
- Card platform readings (H1 the App token creates a draft, H2 the report cap does not reach the create, H3 one ecosystem-and-name entry is the least the endpoint accepts): correctly left to the first live run, as the card's own ⚠️ says; a refusal is a FAILED action carrying `ADVISORY_ACCESS_REMEDY` with nothing re-sent, so a wrong reading costs zero writes. This record does not pre-judge them.
- Tier, for the owning seat: `GOVERNED_SURFACES` on origin/main reads `.claude/**` as Tier S for this repository, and this diff touches no Tier H row (no `.github/workflows/**`). The card and PR body say "Tier H" and ask for a GOVERNED_APPROVERS approval; the register, not the prose, decides, and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green on the head. Noted for the landing step; not a tree finding.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the live tree, trying to break three things the seat weighted: the no-leak rule, the path fence, and "published unreachable".

No-leak, every channel the relay emits on, read in code — holds:
- Payload transport: the workflow on origin/main carries `client_payload` in no step's `env:` (pinned by validate.mjs's event-file battery); both scripts read it from `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`; the run name reads `request_id` alone.
- Validator stdout/step summary: on success it prints request id, target, session and the op NAMES; the payload is printed only under `--json`, which the workflow does not pass. On refusal, every sentence for the draft's keys is closed text: `str` fields print type or byte count, `quiet` lists and enums print `describeQuietly` (type and size), unknown keys are named by key, missing keys by key, the alone fence by op name. The marker-in-wrong-key battery covers `packages` (string and object items), `severity`, `description`, `vulnerabilities` on a draft.
- Executor rows, log lines, step summary, annotation, pace log: `confirmAdvisory` builds `why`/`result` from `advisoryCreateReadBack` and `advisoryCreateLandedText` alone (id and state through `advisoryPrintable`, placeholder when out of shape), plus a platform `message` only when it is one of the six in `ADVISORY_PLATFORM_MESSAGES` (whole-string match); `r.call` is verb and closed path; `rest()`'s `detail` reaches an advisory row only through `advisoryPlatformText`; the annotation message is `action`, `op`, `ghsa_id` and is parsed back before it is emitted. The marker sweep is extended over the draft's runs (created, unconfirmed, wrong-state, 403, 422, refused-before-sending; 32 → 41 runs) with positive controls that the marker did reach the platform body and that `resultOf` would have printed it. The dev's one-time ablation (landed row also printing the summary reds the row case and THE MARKER TEST) is a credible negative control of the right test.
- Seat side: `--json` hands on `{ action, op, ghsa_id }` only; the four draft runs are swept for the marker in every seat line.

Path fence — holds: exactly one new POST path, see ①; the collection's list (GET) is spelled by no row and the whole-table verb pin reds if one appears. Noted, no fix asked: the family regex is anchored on `/security-advisories` rather than on `/repos/{o}/{r}/`, so a tail like `/repos/o/r/x/security-advisories` passes the family; `ADVISORY_CREATE_PATH_SHAPE` refuses it, the table spells no such path, no such endpoint exists, and the family is a pin over the closed table rather than a runtime gate, so it widens nothing.

Published unreachable — holds: the draft's body is built from `summary`, `description`, the mapped `vulnerabilities`, `severity` and `cwe_ids` and nothing else (exact-body pin); `state` is an unknown key on the row; `ADVISORY_REFUSED_STATES` still refuses `published` by name on `advisory_state`; a 2xx that answers any state but `draft` is FAILED, never landed.

Findings:

- should-fix (security-findings.md section 3, bullet 3): "`advisory_report` 只留给 App 无公告写权的仓" names a fallback the relay cannot deliver as written. `tokenPermissionsOf` mints `repository-advisories: write` for `advisory_report` exactly as for `advisory_create` (validate.mjs, "fence grant, accepted side" pinned for all four rows), and the mint step on origin/main fails with zero writes on a grant the installation lacks ("⛔ A refused mint fails this step with zero writes; no step here ever mints an un-narrowed token instead"). So on a repository where the App lacks the advisory grant the report stroke dies at the mint too; ops.mjs's own header still lists "whether a report needs the grant at all" as undecided. The operational outcome stays safe (bullet 4 sends a double refusal to the session hand-off, no account switch), so this is a wording finding, not a leak or a widening. The card prescribed this wording, so the fix is either a reword to what the code does (keep `advisory_report` as the second way in when `advisory_create` is refused; what a report needs is the first live run's reading) or a one-line ruling on the card; either lands in a follow-up on this governed file.
- should-fix (execute.mjs line 192): the header still cites `ops.mjs`'s section "The three rows that touch a security advisory", which this same diff renamed to "The four rows that touch a security advisory" in ops.mjs; a dangling cross-reference between the two authorities. Rename in a follow-up.
- should-fix (.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml, mint comment): "THREE consumers, one at a time" is one row short after this lands; the mint logic is right. Carrier: the next PR touching `fleet-write.yml` (Tier H), as the dev's Acceptance notes say.

No must-fix. The change holds against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against: one op, one quiet field, one POST path, the same stroke-scoped grant, a stricter landing than the report row, and no new spelling of an advisory's text on any public surface.
